_note: JSE syntax-completeness wave 3 — call & loop grammar. Pins: arrow-param DEFAULTS (`(a, b = 5) => …` — the default expression evaluates at CALL time in the CALLEE scope, earlier params and the captured creation scope visible, whenever the arg is missing/null — JSE's ONE missing value) and REST params (`(a, ...rest) => …` binds the remaining args as an array; empty when none) for NAMED params only (destructured `{a,b}` params take neither), call-position spread (`f(...xs)` through every arg-collection path — stored lambdas, user functions, method calls, variadic builtins like Math.max — same iterable coercion as literal spread), and call-on-value (`((x) => x + 1)(4)` / `fs[1](5)` / curried `f(1)(2)` — a lambda VALUE followed by `( )` invokes under the shared 32-frame guard; a non-lambda base leaves the parens unconsumed). Statement-level twins (prefix ++i/--i, for…in over dict keys / array indices) live in the actions corpus.
